title: British Columbia Business Corporations Act guide pack
description: BC company and extra-provincial company guide tracks for annual reports, records, and registry evidence.

content.summary: Home BC companies file within two calendar months after each recognition anniversary. BC extra-provincial companies use their BC registration anniversary.
content.tooltip: Use this guide for BC company and extra-provincial company annual-report tracking.
content.caveat: Annual report and AGM clocks differ. Registration, recognition and annual reference dates must be recorded independently.

content.summary: BC companies keep core records including certificates, orders, securities registers, director records, minutes, resolutions, financial statements, articles, and incorporation agreement.
content.tooltip: Use this guide for BC company records and evidence checklists.
content.caveat: Inspection rights and subtype-specific records can vary.

provenance.changeNote: Reconciled with supplied research register (retrieved 2026-10-04); retained source review metadata; legal approval remains outstanding.

content.summary: First AGM within 18 months after recognition; later AGMs each calendar year and within 15 months of the preceding annual reference date.
content.tooltip: First AGM within 18 months after recognition; later AGMs each calendar year and within 15 months of the preceding annual reference date.
content.caveat: Supported unanimous waiver/deferral must establish the annual reference date; it does not remove annual filing.

content.summary: Meeting ordinary resolutions use a majority of votes cast; written ordinary resolutions use the applicable special majority of eligible votes after circulation to all. Written special resolutions require every entitled holder.
content.tooltip: Meeting ordinary resolutions use a majority of votes cast; written ordinary resolutions use the applicable special majority of eligible votes after circulation to all. Written special resolutions require every entitled holder.
content.caveat: Articles may require a special majority between two-thirds and three-quarters. Pre-existing company rules, class rights, proxies, conflicts and all-shareholder matters need separate assessment.

content.summary: Articles govern quorum; statutory default is two eligible shareholders personally or by proxy, reduced to all when fewer exist.
content.tooltip: Articles govern quorum; statutory default is two eligible shareholders personally or by proxy, reduced to all when fewer exist.
content.caveat: Adopted Table 1 article 8.2 separately requires qualifying persons representing at least 5% of issued voting shares; sole-holder and adjournment rules require evidence.

content.summary: Applicable private BC companies maintain a restricted internal transparency register, confirm annually in the anniversary-to-two-month window, enter awareness changes within 30 days and notify status entries within ten days.
content.tooltip: Applicable private BC companies maintain a restricted internal transparency register, confirm annually in the anniversary-to-two-month window, enter awareness changes within 30 days and notify status entries within ten days.
content.caveat: Prescribed exemptions require evidence. Destroy former-individual records within one year after the sixth anniversary of cessation entry. A future public registry announcement does not establish an active filing duty.
